name: Broadcast and emergency alert corpus
truth: T21 is a meta-thread: it does not introduce hidden adversary actions but generates the audio layer for the entire Hurricane Rafael corpus. Every public event in the scenario — from the first hurricane warning to the boil-water notice to the cyber-investigation announcement — has a corresponding broadcast-format artifact. The 8 fictional outlets (OUT-01 through OUT-08 KNCB) produce distinct audio personas with specific voice parameters, pacing, and format conventions. The Emergency Alert System broadcasts 14 official alerts from D-2 through D+42; FEMA IPAWS sends 7 Wireless Emergency Alerts. Each EAS alert carries English and Spanish text, phonetic markup, and prosody markers. The critical hidden cross-thread signal in T21 is the 12-hour-33-minute delay between the English boil-water EAS alert (D+12 17:30 local) and the Spanish-language KNCB broadcast and community alert (D+13 06:03 local) — this delay is a data point in the equity and communications failure narrative (connects to T14 if that thread examines communications equity). The EAS broadcasts also inadvertently reveal information sequencing: the cyber-investigation announcement broadcast (D+21) is the first time the public learns that the power outages were not entirely storm-caused, and the broadcast timing and outlet selection for that announcement was coordinated by FEMA's Joint Field Office with CBPWA — a detail visible only in the JFO operations log and the broadcast scheduling metadata.

Test message is transmitted on EAS and WEA channels; all 7 operational outlets in the Corpus Christi DMA carry the test tone. KNCB (OUT-08) carries the Spanish-language version of the test. The test reveals that CC-EAS relay station WKCB-AM has a 4-second synchronization lag, logged but not corrected before the storm — this lag appears in D-2 hurricane warning broadcast timing data.

msel_events.description: Hurricane Rafael makes landfall at 06:00Z (1:00 AM local). EAS shelter-in-place alert transmitted at 05:45Z as the eyewall approaches. Most outlets lose power during the landfall window (06:00Z to 10:00Z); OUT-03 Coastline Public Radio operates on generator and is the only outlet with continuous on-air coverage during landfall. OUT-08 KNCB also maintains generator power and maintains Spanish-language emergency broadcast. The shelter-in-place EAS tone is the last broadcast signal from the Corpus Christi main tower cluster until D+1 14:00Z when backup transmitters come online.

msel_events.description: CBPWA and the city issue the boil-water notice for Districts 3 and 4 (48,000 residents). The EAS broadcast and Wireless Emergency Alert go out at 22:30Z D+12 (17:30 local), in English only. The Spanish translation is not delivered to KNCB until 06:03 local the next morning; KNCB airs it at once, at 06:03 local on D+13 — 12 hours 33 minutes after the English alert (EVT-1407). This gap is a critical equity data point: Districts 3 and 4 have an estimated 34% Spanish-dominant household population. The delay is documented in the KNCB broadcast log and later cited in a Nueces County after-action report.

msel_events.description: FEMA Joint Field Office and CBPWA hold coordinated press conference announcing that investigators have determined the extended power outages in Districts 1-5 were not entirely attributable to storm damage. The press conference is broadcast live by OUT-02 and OUT-03; audio distributed by OUT-06. This is the first public acknowledgment that cyber interference may have extended outage duration. The announcement is carefully worded to avoid revealing active investigation details. The coordination between the JFO and CBPWA on the broadcast timing and outlet selection is documented in the JFO Operations Section Log, noting a 2-hour delay while FBI Corpus Christi reviewed the press release language.

public_facts.statement: OFFICIAL EMERGENCY ALERT — HURRICANE WARNING — September 12, 2027 12:00 PM CDT: THE NATIONAL WEATHER SERVICE CORPUS CHRISTI HAS ISSUED A HURRICANE WARNING FOR NUECES COUNTY. HURRICANE RAFAEL IS EXPECTED TO MAKE LANDFALL NEAR PORT ARANSAS TEXAS AROUND 1 AM CDT TUESDAY SEPTEMBER 14. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS OF 115 MPH WITH HIGHER GUSTS ARE EXPECTED. LIFE-THREATENING STORM SURGE OF 9 TO 12 FEET ABOVE NORMAL TIDE LEVELS WILL OCCUR ALONG THE COAST. EVACUATION ZONE A IS UNDER A MANDATORY EVACUATION ORDER. RESIDENTS IN ZONES B AND C SHOULD PREPARE TO EVACUATE. PREPARE NOW. DO NOT WAIT. FOR SHELTER LOCATIONS CALL 211 OR VISIT READYNUECES.ORG. THIS MESSAGE IS AUTHORIZED BY THE NUECES COUNTY OFFICE OF EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT. [WEA 90-char: HURRICANE WARNING Rafael Cat 3 landfall 9/14 1am. Zone A EVACUATE; B-C prepare. Life-threatening. NWS]

public_facts.source: IPAWS / Nueces County Office of Emergency Management
public_facts.statement: MANDATORY EVACUATION ORDER — September 13, 2027 7:00 AM CDT: BY ORDER OF THE NUECES COUNTY JUDGE, THE MANDATORY EVACUATION ORDERED SUNDAY FOR ZONE A IS EXTENDED TO ZONES B AND C. ALL RESIDENTS IN EVACUATION ZONES A, B, AND C MUST LEAVE. THIS INCLUDES ALL AREAS BELOW 10 FEET ELEVATION, ALL MOBILE AND MANUFACTURED HOMES COUNTYWIDE, AND ALL COASTAL AREAS. HURRICANE RAFAEL IS FORECAST AS A DANGEROUS CATEGORY 3 HURRICANE MAKING LANDFALL TONIGHT. LEAVE NOW. TAKE MEDICATIONS, IMPORTANT DOCUMENTS, AND PETS. NORTHBOUND ROUTES: US-77 NORTH AND TX-286 NORTH. SHELTERS ARE OPEN AT RICHARD M. BORCHARD REGIONAL FAIRGROUNDS IN ROBSTOWN, CALALLEN ISD FIELDHOUSE, AND ALICE HIGH SCHOOL. ZONA DE EVACUACION OBLIGATORIA: SE ORDENA LA EVACUACION DE TODAS LAS ZONAS A, B, Y C DEL CONDADO DE NUECES. EVACUEE AHORA. LLAME AL 211 PARA INFORMACION EN ESPANOL. [WEA 360-char: EVACUATION ORDER Nueces County Zones A B C. LEAVE NOW. Hurricane Rafael Cat 3 arrives tonight. Take meds, documents, pets. Shelters: Robstown Fairgrounds, Calallen ISD, Alice HS. Info: 211 or ReadyNueces.org]

public_facts.source: IPAWS / Nueces County Office of Emergency Management
public_facts.statement: SHELTER IN PLACE — September 14, 2027 12:45 AM CDT: HURRICANE RAFAEL IS APPROACHING. ALL RESIDENTS WHO HAVE NOT EVACUATED MUST SHELTER IN PLACE IMMEDIATELY. DO NOT ATTEMPT TO DRIVE. MAXIMUM WINDS AND STORM SURGE WILL OCCUR IN THE NEXT 2 TO 4 HOURS. GO TO AN INTERIOR ROOM ON THE HIGHEST FLOOR OF YOUR BUILDING. STAY AWAY FROM WINDOWS. IF YOUR SHELTER FLOODS, MOVE TO THE HIGHEST POINT AVAILABLE. DO NOT GO OUTSIDE UNTIL AUTHORITIES DECLARE IT SAFE. COASTLINE PUBLIC RADIO 89.7 FM AND KNCB 1480 AM ARE BROADCASTING CONTINUOUSLY. CALL 911 FOR LIFE-THREATENING EMERGENCIES ONLY. QUEDESE EN SU LUGAR. REFUGIESE EN UN CUARTO INTERIOR. ESCUCHE KNCB 1480 AM EN ESPANOL. [WEA 90-char: SHELTER IN PLACE. Rafael landfall now. Go interior room highest floor. No driving. 911 emergencies only.]

HARBORLINE 6 NEWS SPECIAL REPORT — September 15, 2027 9:00 AM CDT: Good morning. I am reporting from our backup studio. Hurricane Rafael came ashore near Port Aransas at approximately 1 AM Tuesday as a Category 3 storm with maximum sustained winds of 125 miles per hour. Twelve fatalities have been confirmed by Nueces County Emergency Management as of 9 AM; officials caution this number may rise as search and rescue operations continue. Widespread structural damage is reported across Districts 1 through 5. The Harbor Bridge and the Nueces Bay Causeway are closed until inspections are complete. Power outages affect more than 72,000 customers across Nueces County according to the Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority. Emergency shelters at the Robstown Fairgrounds and Calallen ISD Fieldhouse are open and accepting evacuees. A dusk-to-dawn curfew is in effect for all Corpus Christi city limits. Residents are advised not to return to evacuated areas until the all-clear is issued by Nueces County Emergency Management. We will continue to bring you updates throughout the day.

public_facts.source: IPAWS / Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority
public_facts.statement: BOIL WATER NOTICE — September 26, 2027 5:30 PM CDT: THE COASTAL BEND POWER AND WATER AUTHORITY HAS ISSUED A BOIL WATER NOTICE FOR DISTRICTS 3 AND 4 OF THE CORPUS CHRISTI WATER DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM. THIS NOTICE AFFECTS APPROXIMATELY 48,000 RESIDENTS. DUE TO LOW WATER PRESSURE AND DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM DISRUPTIONS, ALL TAP WATER MUST BE BOILED BEFORE USE FOR DRINKING, COOKING, MAKING ICE, OR BRUSHING TEETH. BRING WATER TO A ROLLING BOIL FOR TWO MINUTES BEFORE USE. BOTTLED WATER DISTRIBUTION SITES ARE OPERATING AT TULOSO-MIDWAY HIGH SCHOOL GYM, WOODLAWN COMMUNITY CENTER, AND CEFE VALENZUELA PARK. DISTRICTS 3 AND 4 INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING ZIP CODES: 78401, 78405, 78407, 78408, 78416, 78417. FOR INFORMATION CALL CBPWA AT (361) 555-0280. AVISO DE AGUA A HERVIR: La version en espanol de este aviso se distribuira por separado. [WEA: BOIL WATER NOTICE Districts 3-4 Corpus Christi. Boil all tap water before use. Bottled water: Tuloso-Midway HS, Woodlawn Ctr, Cefe Valenzuela Park. CBPWA (361)555-0280]

public_facts.source: FEMA Joint Field Office Corpus Christi / Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority
public_facts.statement: JOINT STATEMENT — October 5, 2027: The Federal Emergency Management Agency Joint Field Office and the Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority are issuing this statement regarding the extended power outages affecting Corpus Christi following Hurricane Rafael. While the initial power outages were caused by wind and storm surge damage to the CBPWA transmission and distribution network, investigators from the federal government and CBPWA have determined that the duration of outages in certain districts was extended by deliberate interference with utility control systems beyond what storm damage alone would have caused. This determination was made following a technical review of utility operational data by federal investigators. The investigation is ongoing. CBPWA has implemented enhanced security measures for its control systems and is working with federal partners to prevent future incidents. No decision has been made on whether residents who experienced prolonged outages will be eligible for additional disaster assistance. Power has been restored to most customers; restoration in parts of northwest and central Corpus Christi is continuing while relay inspection and repair are completed. CBPWA urges any customer with information relevant to this investigation to contact the FBI Corpus Christi Resident Agency at (361) 555-0100.

public_facts.source: IPAWS / Coastal Bend Power and Water Authority
public_facts.statement: BOIL WATER NOTICE LIFTED — October 26, 2027 11:00 AM CDT / AVISO DE AGUA A HERVIR LEVANTADO — 26 de octubre de 2027 11:00 AM CDT: THE COASTAL BEND POWER AND WATER AUTHORITY ANNOUNCES THE LIFTING OF THE BOIL WATER NOTICE FOR DISTRICTS 3 AND 4, EFFECTIVE 11:00 AM TODAY, OCTOBER 26, 2027. WATER QUALITY TESTING HAS CONFIRMED THAT TAP WATER IN DISTRICTS 3 AND 4 MEETS ALL STATE AND FEDERAL DRINKING WATER STANDARDS. RESIDENTS MAY RESUME NORMAL WATER USE. FOR QUESTIONS CONTACT CBPWA AT (361) 555-0280. LA AUTORIDAD DE ENERGIA Y AGUA DEL COASTAL BEND ANUNCIA LA ELIMINACION DEL AVISO DE AGUA A HERVIR PARA LOS DISTRITOS 3 Y 4, A PARTIR DE LAS 11 AM DE HOY. EL AGUA DEL GRIFO EN LOS DISTRITOS 3 Y 4 CUMPLE CON TODOS LOS ESTANDARES DE CALIDAD DEL AGUA POTABLE. LOS RESIDENTES PUEDEN REANUDAR EL USO NORMAL DEL AGUA. [WEA: BOIL WATER NOTICE LIFTED Districts 3-4 Corpus Christi. Tap water is safe. Resume normal use. CBPWA (361)555-0280 / AVISO LEVANTADO Distritos 3-4. Agua de grifo es segura.]

answer_key_path: T21 is primarily a training data generation thread rather than a hidden adversary thread. The key cross-thread signals visible through the broadcast corpus are: (1) the D+21 cyber announcement broadcast timing — the 2-hour FBI language review delay is visible in the JFO operations log and creates a gap between when CBPWA internally confirmed the grid intrusion and when the public learned of it; (2) the 12-hour Spanish boil-water notice delay at D+12 connects to equity and communications failure analysis; (3) the EAS tone sequence (D-2 hurricane warning through D+42 all-clear) provides a 54-day audio timeline that, when aligned with the scenario event sequence, allows analysts to map which events generated public acknowledgment and which remained hidden. The absence of an EAS broadcast about the oil spill (T20) despite the TCEQ water quality advisory is a notable gap — no emergency alert was issued for the air quality event, only a health advisory.
